name: Classic Dry Cider
description: This nonvintage Classic Dry Cider from The Cider Farm is an elegant expression of orchard craftsmanship: it blends five traditional English cider apples with an American tart Liberty apple to deliver firm tannins, balanced acidity, and a clean, refreshing finish. The palate reveals nuanced complexity and crisp effervescence while showcasing the character of true cider apples rather than dessert varieties.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its tactile tannins and vibrant acidity; pairs beautifully with aged cheeses or herb‑crusted poultry.
aroma: bright orchard fruit with subtle tannic earthiness
palate: structured yet refreshing with nuanced apple depth

name: Cyser Cider
description: This lightly golden Cyser bridges the old‑world charm of tart cider apples with the sweet floral richness of locally sourced honey, yielding a semi‑dry libation that still carries approachable warmth. The palate offers a gentle interplay of orchard‑fresh apple and mellow honey that unfolds with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve just chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its honeyed aromatics and pair with nutty cheeses or roasted poultry.
palate: balanced tart‑sweet, soft honeyed texture

name: Dabinett Cider
description: This organically crafted cider from The Cider Farm expresses the noble Dabinett apple in a rare single‑variety form enhanced by select additions of Liberty, Chisel Jersey, and Porter’s Perfection, creating a semi‑dry, floral elegant offering with lush caramel and tropical undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its floral freshness and medium‑plus tannin structure, ideal with creamy cheeses or spiced pork dishes.
aroma: tropical and floral with rich caramel
palate: fresh apple juice, guava and cooked pineapple with balanced medium‑plus tannins

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: This oak‑aged cider unfurls with whisperings of vanilla and toast, the subtle medium‑toast American oak enriching the orchard fruit’s brightness in an elegant, wine‑like embrace. It carries a refined clarity and balance that evokes a polished Chardonnay nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip or white wine glass to highlight its gentle oak nuance: an ideal match for roast poultry or creamy alpine cheeses.
palate: bright orchard fruit with toast

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: A refined and elegant cider gently matured in medium‑toast American oak, offering a soft interplay of vanilla warmth and subtle toast complexity rooted in heritage apple character.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in slender stemware alongside roast poultry or mushroom‑topped fare to uplift the cider’s nuanced oak and orchard fruit interplay.
palate: balanced orchard fruit framed by oak

name: The Cider Farm Belgian Saison
description: This Belgian‑style farmhouse cider unfolds with layered citrus and spice on a background of restrained apple tannins, reminiscent of old‑world saison but refined by orchard depth and aromatic subtlety.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip or stemmed glass to enhance its citrus‑spice perfume and pair with soft cheeses or light seafood fare.
palate: tannic apple with bergamot and gentle hop lift

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Five Year
description: Opulent and orchard‑driven this aged apple brandy offers a refined amber hue and envelops the senses in a gentle embrace of orchard fruit framed by warm oak and bourbon‑barrel whispers each bottle uniquely carries the story of its single‑barrel origin.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to appreciate its depth or with a single small ice cube to soften its warmth; pairs elegantly with rich pâté or aged cheeses.
aroma: deep orchard fruit and charred oak
palate: fruit‑forward with bourbon‑barrel warmth

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Two Years
description: A quietly beguiling Wisconsin apple brandy that speaks in orchard whispers, aged two years in charred bourbon barrels with the subtle presence of wild apple wood from the farm, offering a soft interplay of barrel echoes and orchard purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to admire its clarity and gentle warmth, or use as a refined substitute for bourbon in classic cocktails.
palate: soft apple flesh and gentle oak spice

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Pommeau Aged Three Years
description: A refined and mellow fortified apple aperitif, this Pommeau from The Cider Farm is crafted in Wisconsin using their orchard‑grown cider apples and apple brandy, patiently aged for three years to reveal a soft golden hue and layered orchard fruits
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a small tulip glass as a refined aperitif or alongside nut‑forward desserts, aged cheeses, or fruit tarts
palate: smooth orchard fruit sweetness with a hint of raisin
drinkWindow: drink now to medium term (5 years)

name: Tremlett's Cider
description: This rare American dry cider offers a refined tannic structure and bright acidity that elevate its orchard fruit character into something truly graceful and complex. Aromatic floral top notes lead into a palate marked by green grape, apricot and a whisper of minerality conjuring a gently dusty orchard.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to accentuate floral aromas, lovely with oysters, shrimp cocktail or poached white fish.
palate: green grape, apricot, subtle minerality

name: Tremlett's Cider
description: This artisanal cider presents a beautifully poised balance of tannin and acidity in the old‑world tradition. Vibrant floral and pome fruit aromas gracefully lead into a dry yet gently fruity sip marked by green grape, apricot and apple skin nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip or white wine glass; ideal with light seafood such as shrimp cocktail, oysters, poached white fish and simply grilled poultry.
palate: dry yet fruit‑driven with green grape and apricot
finish: lingering apple skin and subtle minerality

name: La Mission Haut Brion Pessac Leognan Rouge (Full Case Only)
description: Château La Mission Haut-Brion 2016 is a profound Pessac-Léognan built on ripe fruit, broad texture, and exceptionally refined tannins. Richness and power gather through the palate, while freshness keeps the wine articulate and complete.
sommelierNotes: Decant for two to three hours if serving now and pour with roast beef, lamb, or truffle-accented dishes; patient cellaring remains well rewarded.
aroma: Ripe black fruit, cedar, graphite, warm spice
palate: Broad, concentrated, powerful, polished

name: Petit Clos Sauvignon Blanc

sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip wine glass to reveal its citrus and minerality; pairs gracefully with fresh shellfish or as a refined aperitif
aroma: citrus and white flower with chalky minerality
palate: zesty and round with juicy exotic fruit and minerality

name: Domaine Meo-Camuzet Corton Perrieres Grand Cru
description: This 2021 Corton Grand Cru Les Perrières by Domaine Méo‑Camuzet unfurls in refined layers bold yet elegant, melding polished black fruit, restrained spice and a tensile mineral spine that speaks of its stony hillside terroir with poise and promise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar temperature to reveal its structure; pairs exquisitely with roasted red meats or game in rich sauces, and will reward cellaring well into the next decade.
aroma: ripe black cherry, wild blackberry, delicate florals
palate: silky with lingering dark fruit, cocoa, licorice and chalky mineral tension
drinkWindow: From 2030 onward, with long‑term aging potential

name: Pinot Noir
description: A modest Romanian Pinot Noir fashioned under the Dreambird label presents a charming red fruit character with gentle spice framing. name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This Romanian Dreamfish Cabernet Sauvignon evokes a forest’s hush and late‑night indulgence with its modest yet inviting persona, unfolding layers of dark cherry and earth‑tilled tobacco, underscored by a seam of smooth graphite and dusk‑fruited allure. sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar temperature in a simple tumbler to frame its comforting fruit and easygoing structure, a fine match for hearty weekday fare.

palate: vibrant, complex, crisp

name: Spirits 4 Year Old Roknar Bonded Rye Whiskey
description: Far North Spirits Roknar Bonded Rye is an elegant expression of estate‑grown Minnesota grain distilled in the heart of the north. Its nose greets with soft brown sugar and spicy vanilla weaving through warm oak, its body unfurls with polished grain character and gentle anise‑tinged heat, and the finish lingers with subtle star‑anise warmth and a whisper of pretzel salt.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a rocks glass to underscore its soft spice profile, and pair it with smoked ham or nut‑crusted goat cheese to accentuate its savory sweetness.
aroma: brown sugar, spicy vanilla, warm oak
palate: polished grain, gentle anise heat

name: Spirits Agassiz Vodka
description: A quietly refined vodka drawn from Hazlet winter rye grown on the jet‑black soils once bathed by Ice Age Lake Agassiz, this spirit reflects the character of northern Minnesota in its purity and presence, with a subtle nod to Scandinavian clarity and texture, elegant yet resolute in tone.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender tulip glass or martini, the vodka shines alongside clean seafood, light salads or delicate Nordic‑inspired dishes.
palate: silky and rounded with clean grain clarity

name: Spirits Alander Nordic Style Spiced Rum
description: Alander Nordic‑style Spiced Rum presents an elegant weave of hand‑infused Scandinavian baking spices upon a slender, golden rum base, its nose alive with allspice nutmeg clove and ginger‑snap warmth. On the palate it is deftly poised, inviting root‑beer‑like vanilla and peppermint nuances anchored by a whisper of espresso‑mocha, closing with soft caramel and banana‑bread sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or over a large ice cube to accentuate its spice‑cake charm, and pair with hearty ginger‑bread desserts or dark chocolate tarts.
palate: root beer, vanilla, peppermint, mocha

name: Spirits Alander Nordic Style Spiced Rum
description: This Nordic‑style spiced rum unfolds with nuanced warmth: fragrant allspice and nutmeg give way to subtle espresso‑tinged vanilla and butterscotch, finishing with a whisper of caramel and banana‑bread sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or over a large ice cube to admire the spices; excellent with apple‑based desserts or a warmly spiced cake.
palate: espresso‑tinged vanilla and butterscotch

name: Spirits Bodalen Bourbon Whiskey
description: This single‑estate bourbon exudes an elegant balance of bright sweetness and wintry northern character, with estate‑grown Minnesota heirloom corn and AC Hazlet rye offering both warmth and precision. The aroma brings delicate toffee sweetness and citrus zest while the palate unfolds peppery and vegetal tones grounded in wood‑driven depth. The finish is long and rich with lingering dark chocolate and brown sugar.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature neat or with a single clear ice cube so the rye spice and nuanced sweetness bloom with minimal dilution.
palate: Peppery vegetal entry with woodsy depth
finish: Long, rich and persistent with dark chocolate and brown sugar

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: This fearless Navy‑strength gin stands proudly at 114 proof offering a bold tapestry of botanicals. Delicate lavender and juniper weave through hints of yuzu‑like citrus while fennel and licorice add spicy depth and enduring character.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a large clear ice cube in a chilled copa glass lightly twisted with lemon zest or in a bold Gimlet where its intensity holds firm.
aroma: lavender and juniper with citrus lift
palate: spicy fennel and warming rye‑driven heat
drinkWindow: Drink now to enjoy its vibrant proof‑driven intensity

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: A fearless Navy‑strength gin crafted grain‑to‑glass from winter rye in Minnesota this Gustaf offers bold and spirited balance. The aromatic weave of meadowsweet thyme cucumber and vanilla frames an assertive rye‑driven backbone for an engaging contemporary profile.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or lightly diluted to temper its 114‑proof heat, pairing beautifully with a crisp tonic or in a minimalist martini to surface subtle herbal and citrus notes.
aroma: meadowsweet thyme cucumber with a rye‑grain hum
palate: fiery rye warmth softened by fennel citrus pepper and vanilla
finish: dry herbal linger with gentle anise warmth

name: Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey
description: Far North Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey presents itself with a whisper of northern prairie heritage tempered by thoughtful aging. Gentle aromas of brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla bean and freshly sawn oak lead into a plush, butter‑smooth palate with nuanced echoes of smoked ham and soft-baked pretzel. The result is an elegant expression that balances grain‑forward complexity with warming spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or with a single large ice cube to allow its layered flavors to unfurl, particularly in rye‑centric cocktails like a Manhattan or Old Fashioned.
aroma: brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla bean, sawn oak
palate: butter‑smooth, smoked ham, balsa wood

name: Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey
description: An elegant expression of cold‑climate terroir this estate‑grown rye whiskey reveals refined warmth and layered grace. Its character is grounded in rich Minnesota soil and her celebrated AC Hazlet winter rye, offering a balance of gentle spice and soft sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly above cellar temperature to unlock fragrant vanilla warmth. Pairs beautifully with hearty cheeses or spiced autumn desserts.
palate: butter‑smooth with roasted almonds and vanilla

name: Spirits Solveig Anna's Garden Gin
description: This seasonal gin from Far North Spirits unfurls with herbaceous dill at the forefront, tempered by the earthiness of angelica and lifted by zesty lemon notes. Its pale blue hue and delicate profile evoke an early spring garden kissed by morning dew, offering a graceful yet complex canvas for cocktails.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tall, slim glass with a lemon twist or pair with cucumber‑infused tonic to accentuate the gin’s herbal brightness.
palate: earthy angelica balanced with fresh citrus lift

name: Spirits Solveig Anna's Garden Gin
description: A seasonal springtime gin that unfolds bright herbal complexity with a flourish of hibiscus, dill, lemon zest and cardamom awakening the senses with both freshness and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tall Collins glass over ice with tonic or in a light spritz to complement fresh salads or mild seafood dishes.
palate: earthy angelica with cardamom warmth

name: Spirits Solveig Gin
description: Far North Spirits Solveig Gin is an ethereal, contemporary gin distilled grain‑to‑glass from estate‑grown Hazlet winter rye. Vibrant citrus and lavender botanicals mesh with herbal thyme and a whisper of pine in an elegant, refined expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a stemmed Riedel or delicate coupette to appreciate its lifted aromatics or stir into a light gin and tonic with a twist of grapefruit to elevate its brightness.
aroma: citrus and lavender with a hint of pine

palate: Deep yet light-footed, supple, fresh

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: Manotsuru “Bulzai” Ginjo presents a crisply invigorating expression of Niigata’s refined sake tradition, showing delicate citron and yellow apple on the forefront, with a whisper of white pepper and stony mineral, precisely balanced in its ginjo clarity. The nama‑chozo method lends it a bright, zest‑laden energy that evokes the sea‑cooled mornings of Sado Island.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a narrow wine glass to highlight its delicate fruit and peppery minerals; ideal alongside salt‑grilled fish or subtly butter‑seared seafood.
palate: white pepper and mineral briskness

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: This Bulzai Ginjo sake is a refreshing artisan expression from Niigata’s Sado Island crafted by Obata Shuzo under the Manotsuru label, elegantly balancing bright yellow apple and citron notes with a fine mineral undertone. It offers a refined sense of clarity and that invigorating zest one expects from a meticulously milled Ginjo sake.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its bright fruit and spiced nuance; pairs gracefully with delicate sushi or simply butter‑sauteed white fish.
aroma: yellow apple, citron, subtle tropical fruit
palate: refreshing minerality with touch of white pepper

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: This Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake presents itself with an inviting cloudy hue and a light sweetness tempered by gentle sourness. Fragrant notes of starfruit and guava unfold to a refreshing and animated style.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled after an attentive shake to reincorporate the sediment, paired with lively dishes such as spicy Mexican tacos or delicate fried fish to complement its creamy spice.
palate: light sweetness with gentle acidity

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: A luscious Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake, Manotsuru “Countless Visions” unfurls a veil of creamy cloudiness that gives way to a softly sweet, refreshingly balanced palate. Tropical whispers of starfruit and guava interlace with delicate anise and melon, culminating in a gentle spicy crescendo that evokes quiet contemplation.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled after a gentle shake to harmonize its fine rice sediment; beautifully suited to contrast spicy cuisine or to accompany light fried fish for an elegant interplay of texture and flavor.
palate: silky sweet fruit with anise‑melon nuance

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: An elegant junmai sake from Niigata’s artisanal Obata Shuzo, Manotsuru Crane exudes a refined purity with whispering stone fruit and delicate pistachio nuances framed by a subtle kiss of white chocolate. The palate is poised and silky, offering a gently structured yet graceful presence. This is a sake of understated harmony and old‑world craft.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to appreciate its soft fruit elegance or at cool room temperature to reveal deeper umami layers: an excellent companion to sukiyaki or lightly seared tofu.
palate: silky, balanced, subtly nutty

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: This Manotsuru Crane Junmai offers an elegant serenity that whispers of Niigata’s blessed terroir, the clarity of its soft Sado waters reflected in delicate nuances of pistachio and forest floor, its texture pure and unadorned, a quiet embodiment of craftsmanship without flourish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its soft umami and gentle nuttiness, a harmonious companion to sukiyaki, tamagoyaki or subtly seasoned grilled tofu.
palate: mild umami with soft nutty tones
drinkWindow: Drink now to enjoy its fresh aromatic clarity

name: Crane Karakuchi Sake
description: This honjoso sake, Manotsuru Crane Karakuchi, offers a beautifully refined experience with bright citrus florals and delicate almond undertones a silkily elegant expression of Niigata’s dry ‘‘karakuchi’’ tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to reveal its taut freshness or gently warmed to enhance its smooth silkiness ideal with simply seasoned poultry or light seafood.
palate: silky, elegant, dry

name: Daimyo Honjozo
description: This Honjozo from Manotsuru speaks in an understated yet confident voice its gentle refinement reflecting the four treasures—rice, water, brewers and terroir—that define its origin. The palate is dry and soft yet subtly engaging, with airy harmony rather than overt bravado. Drinking it brings a whisper of Sado Island’s misty morning in every sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly warmed or at room temperature to reveal its delicate umami and soften the gentle driest finish.
palate: dry with gentle umami balance

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: A rigorously dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo on Sado Island, “Demon Slayer” delivers a poised mid‑weight presence carving through notes of dried fruit, meadow herbs and a brush of cinnamon, culminating in a crystalline, minerally air of perfection.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled or softly warmed to reveal elegant herb and dried fruit nuances; perfect alongside sushi, fresh sashimi and oysters.
palate: meadow herb and cinnamon mid‑weight

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: An exceptionally dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo’s Manotsuru label this sake presents a crisp clarity with echoes of dried fruit, aromatic herbs and a faint whisper of cinnamon drawing the palate into its penetrating austerity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to enhance its sharp precision and pair with delicate raw seafood or subtly seasoned rich meats to balance the intense dryness.
palate: crisp super‑dry austerity

name: Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daiginjo reveals a delicate interplay of fizz and finesse with lifted notes of ripe melon and lychee carried on a whisper of effervescent silk. It unfolds with gentle aromatic grace and finishes with subtle persistence like the echo of a haiku's last line.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to preserve its soft sparkle, ideally alongside light seafood or elegant hors d’oeuvre to accent its airy clarity.
palate: light, bouncy, gently fizzy

name: Lucky Toki Junmai
description: A pure‑rice junmai imbued with the spirit of Sado Island and the auspicious toki crane it honors. Gentle stone‑fruit and soft white‑chocolate tones glide across a sleek, dry frame with subtle depth, inviting contemplative sipping.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or gently warmed to reveal both its delicate fruit‑like nuance and warming umami: pairs beautifully with sashimi or lightly seasoned fare.
palate: elegant, dry, refined

name: Maho Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Maho Daiginjo presents a lush aroma of ripe peach, orange peel and faint cotton‑candy perfume, giving way to an elegantly mild yet racy entry and a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or about 15 °C in a wine glass to reveal its layered nuance: its gentle elegance pairs beautifully with creamy caviar or rich hors d’oeuvres.
palate: elegant, mild and racy entry

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo
description: Manotsuru “Pure Bloom” Sweet Junmai Ginjo presents a delicate floral elegance grounded in refined sweetness, a soft and light expression born of Sado Island’s pure waters and artisanal tradition. Subtle notes of lychee and cherry blossom drift through its graceful texture, lingering with creamy nuance and poised transparency.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its floral and sweet character, pairing beautifully with creamy desserts or light tomato‑based salads.
palate: soft, elegant sweetness with white chocolate undertones

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo Sake
description: An ethereal and delicate junmai ginjo that feels like spring in a glass offering a soft, floral aroma threaded with subtle lychee and honeyed warmth, its gentle 12 percent spirit carrying a light, elegant sweetness floating on a whisper of vanilla and milk.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its floral nuance: pairs beautifully with light appetizers and fresh summer desserts.
aroma: soft floral bouquet with lychee and honey
palate: elegant, lightly sweet with vanilla‑milk whispers
drinkWindow: drink now to fully enjoy its fresh floral purity

name: Mezcal Artesenal Joven Jaguar Bottle
description: This artisanal joven mezcal is housed in the iconic jaguar‑shaped bottle, an elegant tribute to Oaxacan tradition and design. Crafted with 100 % Espadín agave in Santiago Matatlán, it offers a perfectly balanced smoky character with lively citrus and herbal accents that evoke mineral and cooked‑agave complexity. The polished presentation belies the depth within, making it both a collector’s delight and a refined sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a copa mezcalera at 13 – 14 °C to unveil the smoky, herbal layers. Pair with red meats or bittersweet chocolate to accentuate its dry, herbal finish.

finish: herbal dry linger with refined persistence

palate: smooth, balanced, faint smoke with mineral clarity

description: This Fine Spanish Brandy from Vara caresses the palate with gentle warmth and refined elegance, offering subtle whispers of Medjool dates and toasted coconut alongside a plush, honeyed sweetness and a whisper of saddle‑leather complexity. The solera aging contributes a creamy, rich character framed by soft dark caramel and nutmeg nuances.

name: High Desert Gin
description: A velvety artisan gin that evokes the stark elegance of New Mexico’s high desert. Crafted from a grape‑based high spirit and thirteen botanicals, it greets the nose with juniper and citrus overtones, enriched by sage and anise before revealing a serene, creamy nuttiness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or in refined cocktails such as a Collins or Gin and Tonic to awaken its floral facets; a gentle drop of water or ice unlocks deeper aromatics.
palate: bright citrus with coriander and creamy nuttiness

name: Paso Uno
description: This clear unaged artisan brandy is crafted by Vara Distillery in New Mexico, born from a single alquitara distillation of local wine. It offers graceful pear and floral whispers on the nose, and a smooth medium‑bodied texture with white plum and lily nuances that speak of an elegant unfiltered spirit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or on the rocks to appreciate its fresh orchard fruit and floral clarity, or lengthen with soda or tonic and a twist for a refined aperitif.
palate: white plum, pear, rose and lily
foodPairings: tonic with a citrus peel twist

name: Rum Anejo
description: Vara Rum Añejo is an artisanally crafted New Mexico rum distilled from rich dark molasses and patiently aged to achieve harmonious complexity. Its aromas of caramelized sugar and vanilla glide seamlessly into a palate that murmurs of wood spice, caramelized sugar, and roasted nuts.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a snifter to appreciate its warm, inviting depth or elevate a Dark ’n Stormy with gentle character.
palate: wood spice, caramelized sugar, roasted nuts

name: Rum Blanco
appellation: New Mexico: Vara Winery and Distillery
description: A bright crystalline blanco rum from Vara Winery and Distillery in New Mexico presenting a gentle herbal and tropical fruit bouquet with underlying grassy undertones, the elegantly layered spirit offers an engaging balance that recalls classic white rum tradition while remaining supple and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled or over ice in a highball glass garnished with fresh citrus; works superbly in mojitos mingling mint and lime, or in delicate daiquiris that accentuate its nuanced structure.
aroma: tropical fruit and green herbal lift
palate: earthy balance with clean vibrant character
abv: 40% (estimated typical for unaged blanco; exact not found)
drinkWindow: Drink now through next few years

name: Silverhead Brut
appellation: Ancient Lakes AVA, Washington and Alt Penedès DO, Spain
description: A refined celebration in a bottle, the Silverhead Brut Non‑Vintage glimmers with delicate mousse carrying bright pear, grapefruit and almond aromas. An elegant interplay of creamy texture and lively acidity leads to layered flavors of green apple, chamomile and toasty brioche that linger in a long, graceful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender flutes to preserve its finesse. It pairs beautifully with oysters, lobster mac and cheese or light fried hors d’oeuvres.
palate: creamy mousse, green apple, honeysuckle, brioche

sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an elegant aperitif or alongside richer fare such as roast duck with fig and fennel, or red beet risotto with crispy jamón.

aroma: white peach and orchard fruit with herby lift
palate: focused mineral tension, saline citrus and steely structure

name: Weingut Schatzel Reh Riesling Rheinhessen
appellation: Landwein Rhein (from Rheinhessen, Rehbach parcel in Pettenthal)
description: This NV Riesling Reh from Weingut Schätzel is a quietly bold expression of Rheinhessen: a non‑vintage assembly drawn from the old‑vine Rehbach parcel within the prestigious Pettenthal on the Roter Hang slope. It delivers crystalline Riesling with a lithe texture and an intriguing idea of time in a bottle as new vintages blend with older ones to form its evolving character.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender Riesling glass to preserve its fine acidity and delicate flor‑influenced nuance: pairs elegantly with oysters, citrus‑dressed salads, or subtle fish dishes.
aroma: oyster shell, green almond, chamomile blossom
palate: fluid, slender, deeply salty with autolytic yeast warmth

description: An elegant distillate born of a traditional Alsatian bière de garde, Wolfberger Fleur de Bière NV reveals a delicate perfume of tropical fruits and citrus woven with warm spice and subtle hop florals, all carried on a silky, refined texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve ice‑cold in a slender cordial glass or atop a sorbet for a refined digestif experience.

name: Litchi Neo
description: Wolfberger’s NÉO Litchi is an audacious Alsatian liqueur that captures the refined essence of exotic lychee in a delicately pale‑pink expression. It delivers a silken sweetness underscored by subtle floral and citrus suggestions, an elegant fruit‑forward liquid crafted to enchant aperitif moments or inventive cocktails.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or on the rocks in a tulip glass or mix with tonic or Crémant to showcase its fragrant profile alongside seafood, delicate desserts or fruity pastries.
aroma: floral lychee with rose and jasmine whispers
palate: silky, juicy, gently citrus‑tinged fruit
finish: a soft floral echo with lingering freshness
